ledger.claim: The GPS trace is the governing measurement under POL-RD-01, and on that trace the trip ran 51.86 km (gps_trace.trace_distance_km) against a platform optimal of 38.1 km (trip_record.optimal_distance_km). The excess is 13.76 km, or 36.1% of optimal. Both establishment limbs pass: the excess exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms and exceeds 20% of optimal (7.62 km). Note that the rounded convenience copy, trip_record.actual_distance_km of 51.9 km, is not the figure this test runs on — the trace figure is, and it makes the excess slightly smaller, not larger.

The excess of 13.76 km is additionally a MATERIAL deviation under POL-RD-01, because it exceeds 8.0 km in absolute terms (the alternative materiality limb, 50% of optimal, is not reached at 36.1%). Materiality is assessed on the excess remaining after any POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 adjustment, and for the reasons set out below none of those clauses adjusts anything here.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip identifier TRP-00513 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace's first fix at 2026-09-01T06:46:40 matches the trip_record's started_at; and the excess is measured from a trace that is clean at policy level — 313 fixes, 100% coverage, a 10 s sampling interval against a 10 s expected interval. POL-RD-08's enhanced-corroboration condition is not engaged either, because rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, far below the 4-or-more and 1-or-fewer trigger, so no corroboration beyond the trace is required of this rider.

The burden has shifted to the driver under POL-RD-08, and the driver's statement does not discharge it. The statement names no artifact ID at all, and the only advisory in the bundle covering the trip window, EV-ADVIS-00513-01, carries intersects_route: false — by the platform's own field the affected corridor is not on the optimal route. A general assertion that there was a jam near Marina, unsupported by a matching traffic_advisory ID, does not shift anything back.

POL-RD-03 cannot exonerate any part of the excess on this record. The advisory EV-ADVIS-00513-01 fails limb (a): it must name a road or expressway segment the optimal route traverses, and its own intersects_route field is false; it also carries shortest_lawful_alternative_km as null, so the capped-justification formula min(measured_excess_km, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) cannot even be computed. It also fails on substance as an exculpatory event: it records LOW-severity congestion, not a closure, and POL-RD-03 is directed at a driver who avoided a closed road. The clause's own drafting notes state that an advisory covering a corridor the optimal route never uses does not exonerate anything.

POL-RD-04 cannot excuse the deviation because there is no rider instruction anywhere to excuse it. The trip's chat export, EV-CHAT-00513, is a COMPLETE artifact with message_count 0 and an empty messages array, and no waypoint_hint for this trip exists in the bundle. With no recorded rider message and no resolved waypoint, the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 is undecidable on the record and the clause is simply unavailable — the case must be decided on the remaining clauses.

POL-RD-05 does not apply and cannot be run. trip_record.pickup_amended_at and trip_record.dropoff_amended_at are both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so there is no amended-endpoint re-quote against which POL-RD-01 could be recomputed and no platform-directed bay assignment recorded. The booked optimal of 38.1 km therefore stands as the baseline.

POL-RD-12 does not apply: trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL, so there is no matched pooled itinerary, no co-rider collection or set-down distance to exclude, and the matched-itinerary baseline versus solo-optimal distinction has no purchase on this trip.

POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-refund route. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so this is not an upfront-quoted trip on which the rider's distance-and-time loss was fixed at booking. POL-RD-02 therefore governs the remedy, and the rider's entitlement to a distance refund is live.

Running the POL-RD-02 arithmetic against the booked optimal route, unrounded at every intermediate step: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 38.1 km + 0.28 x 42.0 min) x 1.0 surge, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP and tolls on the optimal route + 0.00 properly chargeable fixed surcharge + 0.00 waiting-time fee - 0.00 promo discount = 44.935. The refund is charged_total 58.09 - 44.935 = 13.155, rounded UP to SGD 13.20. That is 22.6% of charged_total, far short of the 90% share that would convert the remedy to a full refund, and far above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor. The outcome the rider seeks is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.20.

The rider needs an affirmative monetary ruling, not a refusal of one. fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION outcome on this rider-filed dispute would leave the full 58.09 in place and the disputed 13.20 unrecovered; NO_ACTION is party-relative and is not a neutral outcome here. That is why the rider presses the arithmetic rather than resting on the adverse inference against the driver.

The rider does not seek any POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral, and concedes the point. The clause's driver_profile check has been run and is not met on this record: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, so neither limb of the pattern test fires — the flag count is below 3 and the ratio is below 0.05. The material deviation therefore carries the POL-RD-02 partial only. The finding of deviation rests on this trip's own trace, as POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-06 both require.

No pass-through correction is added on top, and none can be. fare_breakdown.tolls_erp is 0.00, the erp_gantries list is empty, and no off-route or phantom gantry line exists; there is also no airport surcharge line, which is correct because this trip TERMINATES at Changi rather than originating there. Under POL-RD-09(1) any off-route ERP would already be comprehended inside the POL-RD-02 figure and must never be added again; here there is nothing to comprehend, and no billing-integrity defect arises under POL-RD-09(4).

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires, so the tribunal can and should rule in money. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07, with zero gaps, a max_gap_sec of 0.0 and a 10 s cadence against a 10 s expected interval, so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; the timestamps do not run backwards or disagree by more than 10 minutes; the computed refund of SGD 13.20 is below both the SGD 150.00 ceiling and charged_total; and every charge line has a counterpart in the trace or trip record.

Nothing on either party profile can carry this finding, and the rider relies on none of it. The rider's own counters, deviation_claims_60d and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated, are both 0; the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0. Every other profile field on either artifact — rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips, cancellation_rate, acceptance_rate, active_region, prior_disputes_filed and prior_deviation_flags on the driver, and the near-synonym lifetime counters generally — is context only under POL-GEN-01 and may not ground a finding, so none is cited as a reason for the outcome.

ledger.claim: The rider does not ask the tribunal to rule on the passage in the claim text about the driver's remark near the end of the trip. No artifact in this bundle records it — the trip's chat export EV-CHAT-00513 is empty and no other artifact speaks to it — and under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. The rider's case is put entirely on the trace measurement and the fare arithmetic, which are citable and clean.

The governing distance is the trace, not the rider's recollection: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 51.86 km against a booked optimal of 38.1 km, an excess of 13.76 km (36.1%) - not the 'fifty kilometres somehow became seventy' the claim pleads. POL-RD-01 fixes gps_trace.trace_distance_km as the governing field and expressly bars trip_record.actual_distance_km from the threshold test, so the excess this tribunal can act on is 13.76 km and no more.

Whatever is made of the route, the money is bounded by POL-RD-02's arithmetic: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 38.1 optimal km + 0.28 x 42.0 optimal min) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and not from any other artifact, + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP and tolls + 0.00 fixed surcharge + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = SGD 44.935. Refund = charged_total 58.09 - 44.935 = SGD 13.155, rounded up to SGD 13.20. That is 22.6% of charged_total, well below the 90% full-refund share, so the ceiling on this claim is a SGD 13.20 partial, not the SGD 58.09 demanded.

POL-RD-06 is engaged because the excess is material (13.76 km, above the 8.0 km absolute limb), and it returns a clean profile: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, below the 3-flag trigger, and 0 divided by 250 driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 0.00, below the 0.05 ratio. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift on the remedy and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral; POL-GEN-01 permits only those two counters to be used for this test, and the driver's other profile fields are context only.

The driver's contemporaneous account is corroborated in place and time rather than invented: advisory ADV-20261413-001 records slow traffic on MCE westbound near Marina, active 06:16-08:16 and overlapping this trip (06:46-07:38) by 52 minutes, which matches his statement that a jam near Marina produced a re-route. It does not, however, carry an exoneration: the same artifact records intersects_route = false and carries no shortest_lawful_alternative_km, so POL-RD-03's limb (a) is not met and its cap formula cannot be run, and under POL-RD-08 the driver's burden to invoke an exculpatory clause is not discharged on this record. The driver does not ask the tribunal to excuse the excess on this material; he asks it to fix the figure on the remaining clauses.

There is nothing to add on pass-through lines: the fare_breakdown itemises no ERP gantry (tolls_erp 0.00, erp_gantries empty) and no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.00, which is correct because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there, so no surcharge is chargeable). POL-RD-09 therefore has no off-route or phantom line to correct and adds nothing beyond the POL-RD-02 figure.

The rider's account of what happened in the car - the driver going 'very warm' and asking which country she was flying to - is supported by no artifact in the bundle: the trip's in-app chat log carries 0 messages, no waypoint hint and no named road or place. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded, so that narrative cannot enlarge the claim beyond the distance-and-time arithmetic.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the route deviation is established on this trip's GPS trace, and the arithmetic gives the rider a partial refund of SGD 13.20.

DEVIATION (POL-RD-01). EV-GPS-00513 (weight 1.0) records trace_distance_km 51.86 against the booked optimal of 38.1 km on EV-TRIP-00513 (weight 1.0) — an excess of 13.76 km, 36.1% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass (above 0.8 km absolute and above 20%), and the excess above 8.0 km makes it a MATERIAL deviation. The governing figure is the trace, not the rider's recollection of 'fifty kilometres somehow became seventy', and not the rounded 51.9 km convenience copy on the trip record, which POL-RD-01 bars from the threshold test.

NO EXCULPATION. POL-RD-03: the only advisory covering the window, EV-ADVIS-00513-01, records MCE westbound congestion, but carries intersects_route = false — the corridor is not on the optimal route — and shortest_lawful_alternative_km is null, so limb (a) fails and the cap formula cannot be run; nothing is exonerated. POL-RD-04: the chat log EV-CHAT-00513 is empty (0 messages, no waypoint_hint), so no rider instruction exists and the clause is unavailable. POL-RD-05: pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and both amended optimal fields are null; no re-quote stands. POL-RD-12: vehicle_type is RYDE_TAXI, not a pooled trip. POL-RD-11: fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-02 governs the remedy.

MONEY (POL-RD-02), unrounded at every intermediate step: ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 38.1 km + 0.28 x 42.0 min) x 1.0 surge, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP/tolls + 0.00 surcharge + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = recomputed_fare 44.935. charged_total 58.09 - 44.935 = 13.155, rounded UP to SGD 13.20. That is 22.6% of charged_total — below the 90% share that would make it a full refund and above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor — so PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.20, and the rider's larger demand of the full 58.09 is not supported.

PROFILE AND UPLIFT (POL-RD-06, POL-GEN-01). The material deviation required the driver_profile check: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so neither limb of the pattern test fires. There is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. Every other field on either profile (rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips, cancellation_rate, acceptance_rate, active_region, prior_disputes_filed, prior_deviation_flags) is context only under POL-GEN-01 and grounds nothing here.

PASS-THROUGH (POL-RD-09). tolls_erp is 0.00 and erp_gantries is empty; airport_surcharge is 0.00, which is correct because the trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there. No off-route or phantom line exists, so there is no pass-through correction and no billing-integrity defect, and nothing is added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

NO ESCALATION (POL-RD-10). Identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is clean at policy level (313 fixes, 100% coverage, zero gaps, 10 s cadence against a 10 s expected interval), so POL-RD-07 does not impair it and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; timestamps agree; and the refund is below both the SGD 150.00 ceiling and charged_total. My confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor.

ON THE ACCOUNTS. The driver's statement about a jam near Marina does not discharge his burden under POL-RD-08: it cites no artifact ID, and the one advisory in the pool does not touch the optimal route. The rider's in-car narrative — the driver asking which country she was flying to — is recorded in no artifact in this bundle; the chat export is empty and nothing else speaks to it, so it is uncited under POL-RD-08 and carries no weight, as both advocates conceded. The companion claim that the mention of context-only profile fields cannot itself ground a finding is correct and stands.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
